Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Uno 2.9.2-1

  • Updated the bundled Uno C++ solver from 2.7.4 to upstream release 2.9.2. Uno 2.9 adds the auto preset (chosen by problem size), function scaling for all methods, a Ctrl-C handler that stops a solve cleanly with the new USER_INTERRUPTION status, and two solution statuses: DIVERGING_ITERATE and UNBOUNDED_OBJECTIVE (which replaces UNBOUNDED). The R-packaging patch set was rebased onto v2.9.2.

  • Updated the bundled HiGHS from 1.14.0 to 1.15.1, the version in the CRAN highs package, with two upstream fixes not yet in a HiGHS release: ERGO-Code/HiGHS#3430 (uninitialized bool members, reported by UBSAN on every QP solve) and #3472 (a container overflow in presolve, reported by AddressSanitizer), the latter moved to its 1.15.1 location. HiGHS’s extern/ extras library is not built: it serves only the HiPO solver, which is off.

  • The status labels uno_solve() returns are now generated from Uno’s C API header at install time, so they follow the bundled Uno exactly; uno_status_labels() lists them.

  • MUMPS through rmumps, two generations: with rmumps 5.2.1-44 or later the package binds to the versioned C interface <rmumps/rmumps_api.h>, whose entry points are named after the MUMPS structure layout they were built for, so a mismatch between the rmumps a binary was built against and the one installed is a clear error when the package loads rather than memory corruption; rmumps 5.9.1-1 brings MUMPS 5.9.1 this way. With rmumps 5.2.1-43 the legacy dmumps_c entry point is used as before. The binding happens in .onLoad. uno_mumps_version() reports the MUMPS reached.

  • New: uno_options() lists every Uno option with its type; uno_solve() gains a name argument (the model name in Uno’s log) and validates the preset; without a log_callback, Uno’s output now goes to the R console through an explicit logger sink.

  • Fixed log_callback, which received Uno’s preamble twice and never the iteration table or the final summary: Uno’s stream buffer expects the callback to return the number of bytes it consumed, and the binding returned 0, which Uno treats as a failed flush. The callback now receives the whole log, once.

  • citation("Uno") now gives a single entry for the R package and points to the references the Uno authors maintain for the solver; the package description cites the published Mathematical Programming Computation paper (Vanaret and Leyffer, 2026) instead of the preprint.

  • Authorship and copyright: Authors@R names every copyright holder of the bundled Uno sources (Alexis Montoison, Joris Gillis, David Kiessling and Manuel Schaich alongside Charlie Vanaret), the package’s own code is attributed to its author, and inst/COPYRIGHTS is self-contained after installation. Uno’s documentation, test suite, AMPL interface, examples and CMake find-modules, none of which the build reads, no longer ship in the source package.

  • Build: Uno is configured with -DUSE_OPENMP=OFF (Uno 2.7.5 made OpenMP the default, which its CMake requires whenever MUMPS is present). The bundled Uno’s CMake gains a FORTRAN_MANGLING_UNDERSCORE option, which the package turns on: BLAS/LAPACK symbol names are spelled with the gfortran convention R uses everywhere instead of being discovered by compiling and linking a Fortran probe, so installing no longer needs a working Fortran link step (nothing in the build is Fortran; R supplies BLAS, LAPACK and the Fortran runtime at link time). For the same reason R’s BLAS and LAPACK link names are handed to Uno’s CMake directly instead of letting it search for libraries the archive never links (the search failed on Rtools without a Fortran compiler). The bundled Uno’s DynamicLoader.cpp includes <cstdlib> for std::getenv, which LLVM 23’s libc++ no longer provides transitively (CRAN’s r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-clang); the 2.7.4-1 fix of VectorView.hpp is moot, that file is gone upstream.

  • Fixed an installation failure on glibc 2.36 and older (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, RHEL 9), where the bundled HiGHS build stopped.

Uno 2.7.4-1

CRAN release: 2026-08-30

  • Fixed a compilation failure with LLVM 23’s libc++, reported by CRAN’s r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-clang check. libc++ 23 dropped many transitive includes in all language modes, so the bundled Uno solver’s VectorView.hpp no longer saw <algorithm> and its use of std::fill failed to compile, taking 28 translation units with it. The header now includes <algorithm> directly. No user-visible change.

Uno 2.7.4

CRAN release: 2026-06-17

  • Fixed the interior-point (“ipopt”) preset on Windows, which failed with “The linear solver MUMPS is unknown”. The shim now resolves rmumps’ dmumps_c via R_GetCCallable (works on Windows) instead of R_FindSymbol (did not), and configure.win builds with MUMPS enabled. Requires rmumps >= 5.2.1-43.

  • Updated the bundled Uno C++ solver to upstream release 2.7.4. The R-packaging patch set rebased cleanly; the C API is backward-compatible and the R binding is unchanged.

  • Build: forward the HiGHS include root into the bundled Uno compile, fixing a “‘highs/Highs.h’ file not found” error from Uno 2.7.4’s prefixed include.

  • Keep the bundled HiGHS/Uno source trees out of the installed package via a top-level .Rinstignore, as CRAN requested; the static libraries are still built from the bundled sources at configure time.

  • Fixed an undefined-behavior report from CRAN’s gcc-SAN / clang-SAN checks (uno_binding.cpp, make_x): a length-0 memcpy received a NULL source. The copy is now guarded; no user-visible behavior change.

Uno 2.7.3-1

CRAN release: 2026-06-11

  • Fixed the bundled HiGHS/Uno source build on non-shlib R (CRAN fedora-gcc/clang, musl): use R.home("include") for R’s header path, and normalize a lib64/ libuno.a install to lib/.

Uno 2.7.3

CRAN release: 2026-06-08

  • Updated the bundled Uno C++ solver to upstream release 2.7.3. The R-packaging patch set was rebased onto v2.7.3; the C API is backward-compatible (the binding is unchanged). One internal fix: Uno 2.7.3 relocated Options::dump_default_options(), so its console output is re-routed through the R-output mechanism (UNO_COUT) to keep the compiled library free of raw std::cout for the CRAN compiled-code check.

  • Added inst/COPYRIGHTS documenting the copyright holders and licenses of the bundled third-party libraries: the Uno C++ solver and HiGHS, including the components HiGHS itself bundles (AMD, METIS, pdqsort, zstr, rcm, filereaderlp, Catch2, and CLI11). All are permissive and MIT-compatible (MIT / BSD-3-Clause / Apache-2.0 / zlib / Boost Software License 1.0); none is copyleft. A Copyright: file inst/COPYRIGHTS field and a cph entry for the HiGHS development team record this in the package metadata. Because the file lives under inst/, the attribution survives installation. MUMPS (reached at run time through the GPL-licensed rmumps package) and BQPD are not bundled.
